instruction: Change the body text font of the document to Times New Roman.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to add page numbers to footers. Opened Insert menu, navigated to Header and Footer submenu, but got stuck in loops between footer deletion dialogs and menu navigation for 50 turns without successfully inserting page numbers.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open LibreOffice Writer menus (Insert, Format), navigate document pages, interact with dialog boxes, access Header and Footer submenu
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to complete the multi-step footer+page number insertion workflow. Got confused by footer deletion dialog, repeatedly toggled footer on/off without inserting page number field. Ran out of turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to font change which requires select-all then font change — fewer steps than footer manipulation. The model showed awareness of the font toolbar area in screenshots.
metadata.explanation: Task asks to change body text font to Times New Roman. Getter reads docx and finds the most common font in body (non-heading) paragraphs. Metric checks case-insensitive match with expected font name.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the docx file and extracts fonts from body (non-heading) paragraphs, weighted by text length, returning the most common font — semantically matches the instruction to check body text font.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter: directly accesses expected.get('expected_font') which aligns with get_rule returning {'expected_font': 'Times New Roman'}.
Case-insensitive comparison is appropriate for font name matching.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Complete coverage: single instruction requirement (change body text font) is fully verified by the evaluator.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: run.font.name may be None if font is set at the paragraph style level rather than on individual runs. Consider also checking para.style.font.name as a fallback. However, the typical workflow (Ctrl+A + font toolbar) sets font directly on runs, so this is unlikely to cause issues in practice.
